title: Add probabilistic latency cascade detector and canary cutoff guard
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context and motivation: We observed a recurring failure mode in canary evaluations where single-percentile alarms (p95/p99) were noisy and often missed multi-percentile cascades: brief shifts where p50 moves slightly but p95 climbs disproportionately due to upstream contention. These cascades often precede broader tail regressions and cause late detection. This PR adds a probabilistic Latency Cascade Detector (LCD) that reasons over the joint distribution of multiple percentiles and identifies correlated, traffic-weighted percentile divergences. The detector is traffic-aware (weights cohorts by recent request volume), applies Bayesian hierarchical smoothing across time windows, and emits a single composite cascade score with explainability fields (dominant-percentile, cohort, and time-window).

What this change does: 1) New detector algorithm implemented in perf-canary service (pkg/detectors/cascade_detector.go) that: - consumes percentile series (p50/p90/p95/p99) and traffic histograms - fits a lightweight probabilistic model (approximate Bayesian change-point + Dirichlet-smoothed percentile mix) - computes a cascade score in [0,1] and a confidence estimate - supports adaptive thresholding by expected traffic and seasonality. 2) Integrates detector with rollout guard pipeline: when cascade_score > threshold for N consecutive aggregation windows, the Canary Orchestrator (orchestrator/canary_guard.go) will pause cutovers and trigger a shadow re-run and a rollback candidate route. 3) Adds lightweight synthetic probe scheduler changes to exercise cohort-level tails more frequently (prober/scheduler.go). 4) Adds dashboards and alerting: Grafana dashboard panels, new Prometheus metrics (perf_canary_cascade_score, perf_canary_cascade_confidence, perf_canary_cascade_root_percentile) and alert rules. 5) Adds end-to-end tests and load tests (tests/e2e/cascade_detector_test.go, perf/load/cascade_simulator.py).

Backward compatibility: The detector defaults are off for existing canary configs; it can be enabled per-policy via the new canary_policy.cascade_detector block. Existing percentile-based detectors remain unchanged. The detector is designed to be additive and to act as an additional guard rather than a replacement.

How it works (high-level): - Input: time-series windows of percentiles and per-cohort traffic counts. - Model: estimate expected percentile mixing using a Dirichlet prior derived from baseline windows, compute a likelihood ratio for the current window under baseline vs delta model, and smooth the likelihood ratio across windows with an exponential decay whose half-life is traffic-adaptive. - Output: cascade_score (probability-like), dominant_percentile (which percentile contributed most), cohort_tag (which traffic slice shows the signal), confidence. - Operational behavior: the orchestrator maps cascade_score -> action using a policy table: low -> annotate and monitor, medium -> pause canary and spin up shadow probe, high -> automatic rollback and notify SRE.

Testing and validation: included are unit tests for the statistical routines, deterministic integration tests with fixed seeds, and a synthetic load simulator to reproduce multi-percentile cascades. We ran the simulator across historical Canary traffic traces (2025 Q4) and compared detection latency to existing p99-only alarms: median detection time improved by ~2.3x on reproductions of cascade regressions, while false positive rate remained within target (<=1% daily on synthetic benign traces).

Rollout plan: feature gated, staged rollout: 1) internal canaries in perf-canary infra (5% traffic) 2) platform QA (10% traffic + active monitoring) 3) opt-in for Redwood-managed canaries 4) automatic opt-in for new tenant policies after 4 weeks if FPs < 1% and no incidents.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of detector algorithm and API hooks
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Load/simulation harness and reproduction cases
- [x] Grafana dashboards + Prometheus metrics + alert rules
- [x] Feature flag and policy toggle
- [x] Documentation updates (docs/canary/cascade_detector.md)
- [x] Rollout plan and runbook

Notes/commentary: This PR focuses on improving detection fidelity for subtle, correlated percentile shifts rather than replacing existing SLO or p99 monitoring. Tunable knobs (window size, half-life, cohort granularity) are exposed in policy with conservative defaults to avoid churn. See docs/canary/cascade_detector.md for algorithmic details and operational guidance.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2026-02-26): Nice approach. Two quick asks: add a comment explaining the Dirichlet prior choice and ensure we don't allocate large arrays per window (GC pressure).
Maya Patel (2026-02-26): Reply: added comments and switched to ring buffer; updated unit tests to validate memory usage.
Ravi Gupta (2026-02-27): Can we add an opt-out at the tenant level? I want customers to be able to keep current behavior.
Maya Patel (2026-02-27): Added canary_policy.cascade_detector.enabled flag and documented it in the policy proto and docs.
Sofia Martinez (2026-03-01): Suggest tuning default half-life to be 3x the aggregation window in low-traffic cohorts; otherwise small cohorts get noisy signals.
Maya Patel (2026-03-01): Adjusted default half-life logic to be traffic-adaptive; added tests that exercise low-traffic behavior.
release_notes: Introduce a probabilistic Latency Cascade Detector (LCD) that detects correlated multi-percentile regressions and integrates with canary rollout guards. Feature is opt-in via canary_policy.cascade_detector and disabled by default; exposes new metrics perf_canary_cascade_score and perf_canary_cascade_confidence.
notes: Merged after two approvals. Canaries for this feature are gated and require manual opt-in during initial ramp. Ops runbook added to docs/runbooks/cascade_detector_runbook.md
